newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Eaton Corp expands S.Korea presence.
newsitem.headline: Eaton Corp expands S.Korea presence.

text.p: While South Korean companies look abroad for cheap labour and new buyers, Cleveland-based Eaton Corp has tapped Korea as a manufacturing center and major market for its products, the company's chairman said on Tuesday.
"The Korean market is a very substantial market," Stephen R. Hardis, chairman and chief executive officer of Eaton Corp, told Reuters.
"I think whenever you enter a market that is competitive, you can succeed to bring in new technology local producers need to compete on a global basis," Hardis said.
More Korean companies are moving offshore because of high domestic wages, rising land prices and excessive regulations.
"Korean manufacturers have obviously ambitious plans to become major global suppliers," Hardis said.

For instance, South Korea's major carmakers -- Hyundai Motor, Kia Motors and Daewoo Motor, a unit of the Daewoo Group -- have global ambitions. But analysts have warned of an impending industry shakeout.

Eaton Corp is a global manufacturer of engineered products that serve the industrial, vehicle, construction, commercial and aerospace markets. It employs 54,000 people at 155 manufacturing sites in 26 counties. Sales totalled $7 billion last year.
"The benefit (of using Eaton products) is always superior technology, and that is the most important thing Eaton will bring to the Korean market," he said.
Eaton Corp will build a wholly-owned plant to produce limited slip differentials, which are used in rear wheel-drive cars and light trucks to improve traction.

The U.S. company is also negotiating with J.C. Corp of Korea, an electric and electronics autoparts maker, for a joint venture to produce automotive controls including convenience switches, climate controls and actuators.
"In today's business climate, it is very hard to make acceptable profits, unless you have superior differentiated products," Hardis said.
He said Eaton would bring several automotive control technologies to Korea.
Eaton was the first North American producer of multiplexed switch systems, which simplify automotive manufacturing by using design enhancements to reduce weight and service costs, he said.
The company also will introduce automatic truck transmissions to Korea, Hardis said.
But Eaton's products will not be limited to the Korean market.

"Whenever we talk about the market today, we always think about markets worldwide," Hardis said. "One of the important reasons to be in Korea is to be able also to work with Korean manufacturers as they go around the world," he said.
Eaton already has invested $7 million in Korea to build a plant to produce ion implanters, a key component in semiconductor equipment.
Eaton's initial investment in Korea would be minimal, less than about $10 million, but was expected to create 300 new jobs.
"In the next five years, we can move into a bit specialty producers that import products into Korea with becoming one of the market leaders in Eaton's product areas," Hardis said.
Hardis said estimated Eaton's sales at more than $100 million this year and $250 million in 2000.
